epics.description: Customers can export their paid orders as a CSV file from their account page. Each order is one row with order number, date and total amount including VAT. Cancelled orders are excluded, and the file name follows orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. The delimiter and encoding are not yet decided.

features.description: Single capability: a customer downloads a CSV file of their paid, non-cancelled orders from the account page.
features.name: Order export

acceptanceCriteria: Given a logged-in customer on the account page, When they trigger the export action, Then a CSV file is downloaded to their device.
Given a logged-in customer on the account page, When the export is triggered, Then the downloaded file contains only that customer's orders.
stories.aiReadyReason: The story relies on the undefined business term 'paid' and does not define the file's content, so the question for the PO is: what exactly counts as a 'paid' order (e.g. payment captured, partially paid, refunded), and which columns must the CSV contain?
dependencies: Export only paid orders and exclude cancelled orders
stories.description: The account page offers an action that downloads the customer's orders export as a CSV file. The export contains the customer's paid orders, excluding cancelled ones. The placement and label of the action on the account page are not specified and are left to the developer.
stories.iWant: to download my paid orders as a CSV file from my account page
stories.soThat: I can keep a record of my purchases
stories.title: Download the orders export from the account page

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer with a paid order and a cancelled order, When they export their orders, Then the paid order appears in the file.
Given a customer with a cancelled order, When they export their orders, Then the cancelled order does not appear in the file.
stories.aiReadyReason: The whole story depends on the undefined term 'paid' (payment captured, partially paid, or refunded orders all change the behavior), so the question for the PO is: what status defines a paid order?
stories.description: Only paid orders are included in the export. Cancelled orders are always excluded from the export.
stories.iWant: the export to include only my paid orders and leave out cancelled ones
stories.soThat: my file reflects only the valid purchases I made
stories.title: Export only paid orders and exclude cancelled orders

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer with two paid orders, When they export their orders, Then the file contains exactly two data rows, one per order.
Given an exported order, When its row is read, Then it shows the order number, the order date and the total amount including VAT.
stories.aiReadyReason: The delimiter (comma or semicolon), the file encoding and the date display format are explicitly undecided, which are choices a developer cannot make, so the question for the PO is: which delimiter, file encoding and date display format should the export use?
dependencies: Export only paid orders and exclude cancelled orders
stories.description: The export contains one row per order with three values: order number, order date and total amount including VAT. The delimiter (comma or semicolon) and the file encoding are not yet decided. The date display format is also not specified.
stories.iWant: each exported order to appear as one row with its order number, date and total amount including VAT
stories.soThat: I can review my orders in a spreadsheet
stories.title: Export one row per order with order number, date and total including VAT

acceptanceCriteria: Given an export made on 2024-05-10, When the file is downloaded, Then its name is orders-2024-05-10.csv.
Given an export made on any date, When the file is downloaded, Then its name matches the pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv.
stories.aiReadyReason: The file name pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv is fully specified, with the date being the download date, and the two criteria are directly verifiable with a concrete example.
stories.description: The downloaded file is named orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv, where YYYY-MM-DD is the date of the export. The file date is the date the export is downloaded.
stories.iWant: the downloaded file to be named orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv
stories.soThat: I can easily identify when the export was made

tasks.description: In the export download flow, generate the file name as orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv, where YYYY-MM-DD is the date the export is downloaded, zero-padded to two digits for month and day. Expected result: an export downloaded on 2024-05-10 is named orders-2024-05-10.csv, and every name follows the pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv.
tasks.title: Build the export filename from the download date

tasks.description: Write automated tests that trigger an export download on a fixed date (2024-05-10) and assert the file name is orders-2024-05-10.csv. Add a test that checks names for other dates match the regex orders-\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\.csv. Expected result: both acceptance criteria pass in the test suite.
tasks.title: Verify the export filename against the acceptance criteria

stories.title: Name the export file orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv
